name: Robot Chicago Pilot Deployment
escalationContact: Moises, who takes it to Robot
trigger: The daily deployment window opens (start time TBD on the source page).
purpose: Robot judges us on what the public sees, and the public escalates. A resident photographed roughly a dozen bots lined up on a public sidewalk at night and posted it, tagging Robot, a community account and the 43rd Ward alderman. Every rule here is downstream of that: 2 at a time, 4 per merchant, nothing staged in bulk in public, no prep where people can see it. Pilot deployment only, where bots drive themselves out under pilot control; van and truck deployment is a different, undocumented process.
doneWhen: Every bot is deployed and clear, no merchant is over 4 bots, and nothing is left sitting in public.

steps.title: Power on the bots and run the health check
steps.trigger: The daily deployment window opens, with the plan checked against the 4-bot cap and batteries and supplies staged inside the secure area.
steps.work: Power on every bot in the deployment set and run the health check on each one. What the health check covers is TBD for the owner to fill in.
steps.doneWhen: Every bot in the set has a pass or fail recorded.

steps.title: Fix it on the spot, or ground it?
steps.owner: Moises / NO crew on the ground
steps.trigger: A bot failed the health check.
steps.work: Check both: it is a tier 1 repair, and it needs no part or you have the part on you. Never send out a bot that failed the check and was not fixed; that becomes a grounded bot in public, which is the thing this Automation exists to prevent. Where the tier 1 repair list is documented is TBD, and without it a new person cannot run this decision.
rules: Never send out a bot that failed the check and was not fixed.
steps.doneWhen: Every bot is either passing or grounded, with none in between.

steps.title: Ground the bot
steps.trigger: A failed bot is not a tier 1 repair, or the part is not on hand.
steps.work: The bot does not go out. It is handled under Step 5 of the Undeployment Automation: moved into the private secure area for the pickup team, never staged on the sidewalk.

next.label: Continue with the rest of the set

steps.title: Ping Moises about the failure
steps.trigger: You cannot tell whether a failure is a tier 1 repair.
steps.work: Ping Moises with the bot ID, what failed, and the part you think it needs. The bot stays grounded while you wait.

steps.title: Clean and swap batteries if it wasn't done last night
steps.trigger: The set's passing bots are identified.
steps.work: Clean and battery swap any bot that did not get cleaned and swapped the night before. Do this inside the private secure area. Never swap batteries or prep bots where the public can see it, especially in quantity.
rules: Never prep or swap batteries where the public can see it.
steps.doneWhen: Every bot going out is clean and on a good battery.

steps.title: Stage each bot nose-in
steps.trigger: Bots are clean and on good batteries.
steps.work: Park each bot facing into the sidewalk, not facing the street, so the pilot's first move is forward. Rolling a bot forward is faster than backing it up because of how you have to tip it, so the crew's instinct is to park at the curb facing out. Do it the other way. This takes mistakes out of the pilot's hands, so it applies to pilot deployment only.
steps.doneWhen: Every staged bot can pull straight forward onto the sidewalk with no reversing.

steps.title: Is the departure path clear of standing water?
steps.work: Look at the path each bot will take leaving the stage point. Never let a bot drive through standing water; it damages the base. Water on the path is a hard stop, not a judgment call about how deep it looks.
rules: Never let a bot drive through standing water.

steps.title: Restage and ping Moises
steps.trigger: No dry path exists to leave the stage point.
steps.work: Do not send the bot. Restage it and ping Moises.

steps.title: Send trips to no more than 2 bots
steps.trigger: A pair of bots has a dry departure path and the merchant is under the 4-bot cap.
steps.work: Send trips to 2 bots, not the whole set. Never send trips to more than 2 at a time, never stage more than 2 together in the public right of way (including when staging for GPS or signal), and never put more than 4 bots at any one merchant. We used to blast the whole set of 15 or 20 and let pilots drive them away as they became active; that is the old process. If the plan would put a fifth bot at a merchant, do not send it: reassign or hold, and ping Moises, since the cap is Robot's.
rules: Never send trips to more than 2 bots at a time.
Never stage more than 2 bots together in the public right of way.
Never put more than 4 bots at any one merchant.
steps.doneWhen: Exactly 2 bots have trips and are moving, and no merchant is over 4 bots.

steps.title: Are both bots out of sight?
steps.trigger: A pair has trips and is moving.
steps.work: Watch the pair leave. Cleared means out of sight; never start the next pair because the first is basically gone. If too many bots are already staged in public because a pair has not cleared, stop sending and wait. Target state is Stella making this call off the map instead of a person, which is not live yet.
rules: Out of sight is the bar for starting the next pair.
